deep.reconstruction:
Context: Problem III (§10) asks for all prime divisors D of numbers p^2+nq^2 with gcd(p,q)=1 and gcd(p,n)=1. On the previous page Euler, following Lagrange, shows that every such D is represented by a reduced binary form D=fr^2+2grs+hs^2 with fh-g^2=n and 2|g|<=f,h, so that g<sqrt(n/3). From the identity Df=(fr+gs)^2+ns^2 he concludes that D·f is represented by the principal form x^2+ny^2. The same holds for D·h.

This page, I: list the finitely many admissible leading coefficients f, f', f'', ... of reduced forms of determinant n. Every prime divisor D then satisfies: D, or Df, or Df', ... is of the form p^2+nq^2. Euler credits this to Lagrange.

II: He combines this with his own older results (E164 and related papers). The prime divisors of p^2+nq^2 lie in residue classes 4ni+a, where the a's are exactly half of the residues mod 4n that are coprime to 4n. The other half, the α's, contain no divisors at all. As partial justification he notes:
- If D=p^2+nq^2 with q even, then D ≡ p^2 (mod 4n).
- If q is odd, then q^2 ≡ 1 (mod 8), hence nq^2 ≡ n (mod 4n) and D ≡ p^2+n (mod 4n).
So the a-set contains the odd squares coprime to 4n and the numbers p^2+n coprime to 4n. He asserts that the cases where only Df is principal give 'the same numbers', to be shown in examples.

III: Proposed sieve. Remove from 4ni+a every number divisible by some number ≡ α. If one could prove that the α-classes contain all primes that are not divisors, then every prime ≡ a would be a divisor. He states that the whole question reduces to this. In modern terms, this is the statement that the set of primes p with (-n/p)=1 is a union of residue classes mod 4n forming an index-2 subgroup. That is quadratic reciprocity, including its supplementary laws.

§11 (Corollary 1): the φ(4n)=2λ reduced residues split into λ a's and λ α's. The next page adds that the a's form a subgroup and the α's form its coset.
errors: The assertion that the residues a are exactly the odd squares together with the p^2+n, and that the cases where Df (with f≠1) is principal yield 'the same numbers', is false in general. These two families only give the residues of numbers represented by the principal form, i.e. the principal genus. Primes represented by non-principal genera fall in other classes. Example n=5: the a-classes mod 20 are {1,3,7,9}, but squares and p^2+5 give only {1,9}. The prime 3 (with 3·2=6=1+5) lies in class 3. Euler defers this point to 'examples', and it is a genuine gap/error.

Section III's reduction is circular as a proof strategy. The claim that the α-classes contain all non-divisor primes is exactly the hard content: the converse direction of quadratic reciprocity. Euler admits he cannot prove it; it remained open until Gauss (1796/1801).
Minor: the equality of the class sizes (λ each) is asserted, with only a hint ('facile demonstrari potest') given on the next page.

ideas.what: Every prime divisor D of p^2+nq^2 is such that D·f is represented by x^2+ny^2 for some leading coefficient f of a reduced form of determinant n.
ideas.modern_name: Reduction theory of positive definite binary quadratic forms; finiteness of form classes; composition with the principal form

ideas.what: Prime divisors of p^2+nq^2 lie in exactly half of the reduced residue classes mod 4n (the a-classes); the α-classes contain no divisors.
ideas.modern_name: Dependence of the Legendre symbol (-n/p) on p mod 4n; quadratic character / Kronecker symbol; quadratic reciprocity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (conjectured in E164 and later papers; E744), proved by Gauss 1801
ideas.where_published: E164 (Theoremata circa divisores numerorum in hac forma paa±qbb contentorum), E744 and others

ideas.what: The residues of numbers of the form p^2+nq^2 mod 4n are the odd squares and the squares plus n, using q^2≡1 mod 8 for odd q.
ideas.modern_name: Principal genus / values of the principal form mod 4n
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler; genus theory systematized by Lagrange, Legendre, Gauss
ideas.where_published: Similar computations in E164 and E256-era papers

ideas.what: Sieve reduction: exclude from the a-classes all multiples of α-numbers; the full theory then reduces to proving that all non-divisor primes lie in the α-classes.
ideas.modern_name: Reformulation of the converse of quadratic reciprocity
ideas.where_published: E598; cf. Weil, Number Theory: An Approach through History

ideas.what: The a-classes and α-classes have equal size λ = φ(4n)/2.
ideas.modern_name: Kernel of a quadratic character is a subgroup of index 2 in (Z/4nZ)^*

deep.surprise_reason: This is Euler's well-documented late synthesis of Lagrange's reduction theory with his own residue-class conjectures, which amount to quadratic reciprocity. It is discussed by Weil and others. The only notable detail is an error: he claims that non-principal representations give 'the same' residues, which overlooks genus distinctions. Nothing on the page is new.
transcription_corrections: Corollary 1: '(semper enim iste numerus est par). Prior forma a continet' — the full stop is better read as a comma or semicolon continuing the sentence.
Otherwise the transcription agrees with the image (e.g. 'sum commentatus', 'D = 4ni + pp + n', 'Nn 2').
